title: Typical success
note: Upright positions in labor. The 3-shot rewrite drops from grade 15+ to about grade 8, keeps the main findings and the call for more research, and the checker finds every sentence supported.

title: Error the checker catches: invented detail
note: The rewrite claims benefits in “four out of these six groups.” The abstract never splits results that way. The checker flags it twice: the number 4 is not in the source, and the support score is 0.01. Click the flagged sentence to see the closest source text.

title: Error the checker catches: certainty raised
note: The abstract says family intervention “may decrease” relapse. The rewrite says it “helped reduce” relapse and adds “95%” to a confidence interval the source reports without it. Flagged with a support score of 0.01.

title: Error the checker misses
note: The source says other therapies “would seem to be preferable.” The rewrite says “doctors usually recommend other types of talk therapy that have been shown to work well,” which invents a practice claim and raises certainty. The checker gives it 0.67 and does not flag it. An unflagged sentence is not guaranteed correct.

title: False alarm: a correct conversion
note: The source gives risk ratios of 0.91 and 0.87; the rewrite correctly turns them into “9% lower” and “13% lower.” The number rule flags 9 and 13 because they never appear in the source. Derived numbers are a known weakness of the rule.

title: False alarms on paraphrase
note: Interferon for hepatitis C. The key result (17 in 100 cleared the virus vs 3 in 100) is correct and passes. But “taking more interferon or keeping it up for longer also seemed to help” is flagged with a score of 0.01, even though the source says higher doses and longer treatment were more effective: the NLI model misses loose paraphrases.

title: Baseline failure: main finding dropped
note: The extractive baseline keeps the 3 sentences with the fewest numbers. The main finding (text-message reminders improved attendance) contains numbers, so it is dropped. Every kept sentence is copied from the source, so the checker cannot see the omission.
